newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK August PSBR data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK August PSBR data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK August public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) data showing a budget deficit of 4.53 billion stg.
The market consensus forecast was for an August PSBR of 4.1 billion stg .
"Slightly disappointing, especially if you consider there are privatisation proceeds in there as well. The underlying picture is still pretty disappointing."

"They are slightly disappointing. The fact that privatisation receipts acutally came in a little higher than we had anticipated also tends to suggests that the underlying improvement may not be quite as good as we thought after the July data. It probably helps the interest rate markets a little bit and maybe a small negative for the pound."

"Quite disappointing, but as always we find something encouraging, which is that government spending came in slightly better than expected. All the damage this month was on the receipts side, particularly VAT...I still think we're on target to roughly meet the government's 27 billion stg target for the year as whole."
MARIAN BELL, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"A higher than forecast 4.5 billion stg August PSBR is gilt negative, particularly since privatisation proceeds were also higher...After July's unexpected improvement, this will cast new doubt on the Chancellor's ability to hit even the upwardly revised set of ex-privatisation proceeds PSBR of 31.4 bln stg for the full year."
